A choice for the square

Imagine that Town Square has space for one afternoon activity. Which would you recommend, and what would help more neighbors join?

This practice exercise takes inspiration from Poll Voting, credited to @maxigram in the historical inventory (page 16). The choices below are fictional. Nothing is submitted, counted or scheduled.

Compare three options

  • Story circle: Everyone can join while seated, and it needs no supplies. Ask speakers to take turns, and provide a written prompt for anyone who prefers to read or write.
  • Paper craft table: Visitors can arrive in their own time and follow written or spoken steps. The table needs space, paper, and a way to join without folding or cutting.
  • Photo walk: People can notice details together without taking photos. Some may prefer to stay in one place, so consider a seated way to describe what the walkers find.

Make a recommendation

  1. Pick a priority: easy to join, few supplies, or flexible arrival.
  2. Choose one activity. Say or write why it fits your priority and name one change that would help someone who might otherwise miss out.
  3. Try a different priority. Would you choose the same activity? Explain what changed or what still matters most.
Read a worked example

With few supplies as my priority, I’d choose the story circle and ask someone to read the prompt aloud and offer a copy to read. If arriving at any time mattered more, I’d choose the craft table with one short exercise and an option to describe the design aloud.
